subject: Private hotpatch orchestration + circuit-breaker ladder for 2028.10.12 maintenance
body:
From: ops-engineer@acmehealth.com
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai
Cc: tim.owens@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 3 Oct 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private fleet patch - ACME request + constraints

Hi Lukas,

We need to schedule a maintenance to apply a critical kernel and runtime hotpatch on our private Redwood deployment in us-west-2 (VPC). Targeting 2028-10-12 as the earliest possible date. Constraints:
- Production footprint: 24 GPU nodes behind two LB pools (canary pool ~10% of traffic).
- Business blackout: no changes during weekday 14:00–18:00 PT (billing cutover).
- We require a documented rollback path, and a 2-hour SLA for full service restore if the patch fails.
- Compliance wants a preflight checklist and artifact hashes before cutover.

Can Redwood propose a runbook that includes a staged canary, KV-cache drain, and automated circuit-breaker to abort and revert? Also list the expected downtime for each stage.

Thanks,
Raj (ACME Ops)

---

From: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai
To: ops-engineer@acmehealth.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 3 Oct 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private fleet patch - ACME request + constraints

Raj,

Thanks — proposed plan attached (private-hotpatch-runbook-v1.2.pdf) and a preflight checklist (staging-preflight-checklist.xlsx). High level:

1) Preflight (48–24h before)
   - Validate artifact hashes and upload to customer bucket (we'll provide signed URL).
   - Run staging smoke tests against a mirrored staging cluster; collect canary-metrics-baseline.csv.
   - Confirm rollback image is pinned in registry and accessible.

2) Maintenance window (2028-10-12, 06:00–12:00 PT preferred)
   - Phase A (Canary): drain 10% pool -> apply runtime patch -> smoke + latency profile (15–20 min).
   - Phase B (Staggered pool update): update one LB pool at a time with 15m soak per machine.
   - Phase C (Full fleet sweep): parallel rolling update with KV-cache warmup.

3) Circuit-breaker ladder (automated triggers)
   - Level 1: Canary error rate >2x baseline for 5m -> halt rollout and alert on-call.
   - Level 2: Latency increases beyond SLO (p95 > 2x baseline) for 10m -> auto-roll back canary to prior image.
   - Level 3: Severe: service degradation persists after rollback -> failover to Dedicated fallback pool and initiate full restore runbook.

Rollback options described: image rollback, config revert, and as last resort, re-provision last-known-good AMI. Expected median restore from rollback: 18–25 minutes (image swap + health checks).

Notes/asks for ACME: please confirm the allowed 06:00–12:00 PT window (we avoid your billing blackout), share bucket ACL for artifact staging, and confirm that network ACLs allow preflight test IPs.

Attachments: private-hotpatch-runbook-v1.2.pdf (runbook), staging-preflight-checklist.xlsx (check matrix), canary-metrics-baseline.csv (staging metrics snapshot)

— Lukas
Site Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

---

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 3 Oct 2028 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private fleet patch - ACME request + constraints

Couple of operational details to add into the runbook:

- KV cache handling: explicit snapshot then TTL refresh. We should force a KV cache flush on the canary nodes and then rerun warmup probes to avoid cold-start latency spikes.
- Model pinning: any model weights referenced in config must be pinned to the digest; add a validation step in preflight to assert pin immutability.
- DB migrations: zero-downtime expectation — if there is an offline migration, it needs explicit approval and its own rollback plan.
- Health checks: add a 3-tier health check (app, model-serving, infra). If model-serving fails but infra is healthy, we should route traffic off to fallback model variant before full rollback.

I'll add these as a v1.3 diff in the runbook. Also recommend a hard cutover timeout of 45 minutes per node during full sweep to avoid cascading queues.

— Dev
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

---

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 4 Oct 2028 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private fleet patch - ACME request + constraints

Quick add: rollback ladder needs a manual confirmation gate at Level 2 before we proceed to full fleet rollback. Automation should attempt a rollback, but require operator confirmation for fleet-wide actions (20m human acknowledge window).

Also: telemetry retention for the window should be bumped to 90 days for postmortem (per compliance ask). We will surface a deck of dominant error signatures to ACME after the event.

I'll coordinate on-call shifts; recommend Monica take primary for this run.

— Soojin
Director, Private Deployments

---

From: tim.owens@acmehealth.com
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ops-engineer@acmehealth.com, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 4 Oct 2028 17:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private fleet patch - ACME request + constraints

Lukas, Dev, Soojin — thanks for the thorough plan. ACME can accept the 2028-10-12 06:00–12:00 PT window. We confirm:
- Bucket ACL: shared; you should have read/write with signed URLs (I uploaded the artifact hashes).
- Network: we'll open required preflight IPs for 48h before the window.
- Compliance: telemetry retention change approved for the temp window.

We reviewed attachments and the canary baseline. Please proceed with the staging preflight by EOD Friday and provide the v1.3 diff from Dev when available. Monica — Tim asked you to share the on-call roster and point-of-contact for rollback confirmations.

Regards,
Tim Owens
Head of Platform Engineering, AcmeHealth
